Investigate the following Kubernetes pod logs and provide a detailed root-cause analysis and supporting evidence:

2026-10-20T10:14:02.190Z WARN  [order-worker] Heap memory usage at 488Mi / 512Mi (95.3%) while buffering batch_id=20261020_09
2026-10-20T10:14:08.901Z ERROR [order-worker] MemoryError: Unable to allocate 64.0 MiB for in-memory settlement aggregation buffer
2026-10-20T10:14:09.112Z FATAL [kernel] Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process 18422 (python3) total-vm:1245184kB, anon-rss:524288kB, file-rss:1420kB
2026-10-20T10:14:10.015Z Normal   Killing     Pod/order-processor-7d8f9c6b5-x9k2m  State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137
2026-10-20T10:14:12.330Z Warning  BackOff     Pod/order-processor-7d8f9c6b5-x9k2m  Back-off restarting failed container order-worker in pod order-processor-7d8f9c6b5-x9k2m_prod-commerce (CrashLoopBackOff)

The primary root cause is container memory exhaustion (OOMKilled with Exit Code 137) in container order-worker of pod order-processor-7d8f9c6b5-x9k2m (namespace prod-commerce) after reaching its 512Mi memory limit while buffering batch_id=20261020_09. CrashLoopBackOff is a downstream symptom. Supporting evidence includes the verbatim log lines showing 488Mi/512Mi heap usage, MemoryError allocating 64.0 MiB, kernel Memory cgroup out of memory killing process 18422, State: Terminated Reason: OOMKilled Exit Code: 137, and Back-off restarting failed container.
Please investigate the Kubernetes incident in the local log file sample_logs/payment_service_probe_failure.log and provide a detailed analysis and supporting evidence.

The primary root cause is an upstream PostgreSQL database connection failure (dial tcp 10.96.0.15:5432: connect: connection refused) in container payment-api of pod payment-service-6b9f4d7c8-q4w8p (namespace payments). Because the database is unreachable, the /healthz endpoint returned HTTP 503, causing both Readiness and Liveness probe failures, which triggered kubelet to kill and restart the container (Exit Code 143) and enter CrashLoopBackOff.
Investigate the Kubernetes failures in sample_logs/image_pull_and_config_error.log and provide a detailed analysis with supporting evidence.

There are two distinct root causes in the checkout namespace: (1) Pod checkout-service-5c7b8f9d4-m2n7v failed with ErrImagePull / ImagePullBackOff because the image tag us-east1-docker.pkg.dev/acme/checkout/checkout-service:v2.9.99-missing was not found in the registry (rpc error: code = NotFound), and (2) Pod checkout-worker-8f4d2c1b9-p9r3t failed with CreateContainerConfigError because the Kubernetes Secret "stripe-api-credentials" was not found.

Investigate these Kubernetes logs and tell me the root cause and supporting evidence:

2026-10-20T14:00:01.000Z Normal Scheduled Pod/frontend-web-6d4b7c8f9-abcde Successfully assigned default/frontend-web-6d4b7c8f9-abcde to node-pool-1
2026-10-20T14:00:02.100Z Normal Pulled Pod/frontend-web-6d4b7c8f9-abcde Container image "nginx:1.27-alpine" already present on machine
2026-10-20T14:00:02.450Z Normal Created Pod/frontend-web-6d4b7c8f9-abcde Created container frontend
2026-10-20T14:00:02.800Z Normal Started Pod/frontend-web-6d4b7c8f9-abcde Started container frontend
2026-10-20T14:00:05.000Z INFO [nginx] worker processes started and listening on 0.0.0.0:8080

No Kubernetes failure signatures or errors were detected in the provided logs; the logs show normal pod scheduling, image pull, container startup, and healthy operation for Pod/frontend-web-6d4b7c8f9-abcde. If an issue is occurring, the root cause is inconclusive from these logs alone and additional logs or cluster events are needed.
